characters.name: Jesus
characters.note: Risen teacher who appears to the apostles in Acts 1 and is preached throughout the book; appears in person only in the Acts 1 ascension and in Saul's vision (Acts 9, 22, 26).

characters.name: Theophilus
characters.note: Addressee of the book; named only in Acts 1:1 and not present in any scene.

characters.name: Peter
characters.note: Apostle, fisherman of Galilee, leader of the Jerusalem disciples in Acts 1-12; preaches, heals and speaks at the council; distinct from Simon the tanner and Simon the sorcerer.

characters.name: John
characters.note: Apostle, companion of Peter in Acts 1-4, 8; not to be confused with John Mark or John the Baptist.

characters.name: James
characters.note: Apostle executed by Herod in Acts 12:2; not to be confused with James the brother of Jesus.

characters.name: James the brother of Jesus
characters.note: Leader of the Jerusalem assembly who speaks at the council (Acts 15) and receives Paul (Acts 21); distinct from James son of Zebedee.

characters.name: Andrew
characters.note: Apostle named only in the list of Acts 1:13; does not act.

characters.name: Philip the apostle
characters.note: One of the apostles in the upper room (Acts 1:13); distinct from Philip the evangelist, one of the seven.

characters.name: Thomas
characters.note: Apostle named only in the list of Acts 1:13; does not act.

characters.name: Bartholomew
characters.note: Apostle named only in the list of Acts 1:13; does not act.

characters.name: Matthew
characters.note: Apostle named only in the list of Acts 1:13; does not act.

characters.name: James son of Alphaeus
characters.note: Apostle named only in the list of Acts 1:13; does not act.

characters.name: Simon the Zealot
characters.note: Apostle named only in the list of Acts 1:13; does not act.

characters.name: Judas son of James
characters.note: Apostle named only in the list of Acts 1:13; does not act.

characters.name: Judas Iscariot
characters.note: Former apostle who betrayed Jesus; his death is described by Peter in Acts 1:16-20; does not appear on stage.

characters.name: Mary the mother of Jesus
characters.note: Mother of Jesus, named in the upper room gathering of Acts 1:14; does not speak.

characters.name: Matthias
characters.note: Chosen by lot to replace Judas (Acts 1:23-26) and counted with the eleven.

characters.name: Joseph called Barsabbas
characters.note: Candidate put forward with Matthias to replace Judas (Acts 1:23); not chosen.

characters.name: Two men in white clothing
characters.note: Heavenly messengers who speak at the ascension (Acts 1:10-11).

characters.name: Holy Spirit
characters.note: Divine presence acting in the book, descending at Pentecost (Acts 2) and directing missionaries; appears as tongues of fire and wind.

characters.name: God
characters.note: God, who speaks and acts through angels, prophets and the Spirit; appears in Stephen's vision and in Paul's speeches; not depicted in human form.

characters.name: Crowd at Pentecost
characters.note: Diaspora Jews and proselytes gathered in Jerusalem who hear the disciples speak in their own languages (Acts 2:5-13).

characters.name: The eleven apostles
characters.note: The company of apostles acting together in Jerusalem (Acts 1-2, 4-6); they speak as a body at points.

characters.name: The assembly of disciples in Jerusalem
characters.note: The believing community in Jerusalem who pray, share goods and gather in the temple (Acts 2-5).

characters.name: The council
aliases: the senate of the children of Israel
characters.note: Jerusalem ruling council that arrests and examines the apostles (Acts 4-5, 6, 22-23).

characters.name: Annas the high priest
characters.note: Elder high priest present at the trial of Peter and John (Acts 4:6); distinct from later high priests of the same title.

characters.name: Caiaphas
characters.note: Priest named at the trial of Peter and John (Acts 4:6); does not speak.

characters.name: The lame man at the Beautiful Gate
characters.note: Beggar healed by Peter and John at the temple gate (Acts 3:2-10).

characters.name: Ananias
characters.note: Believer who lies about his land sale and dies (Acts 5:1-5); not to be confused with Ananias of Damascus or Ananias the high priest of Acts 23.

characters.name: Sapphira
characters.note: Wife of Ananias who lies with him and dies (Acts 5:1-10).

characters.name: Gamaliel
characters.note: Pharisee teacher of the law who urges the council to release the apostles (Acts 5:34); also Paul's teacher (Acts 22:3).

characters.name: Theudas
characters.note: Rebel leader mentioned in Gamaliel's speech (Acts 5:36); does not appear on stage.

characters.name: Judas of Galilee
characters.note: Rebel leader of the census days mentioned in Gamaliel's speech (Acts 5:37); does not appear on stage.

characters.name: Stephen
characters.note: One of the seven chosen to serve tables (Acts 6:5), preacher and first martyr, stoned in Acts 7; distinct from no one else of that name.

characters.name: Nicolaus of Antioch
characters.note: One of the seven chosen in Acts 6:5; named only, does not act.

characters.name: Prochorus
characters.note: One of the seven chosen in Acts 6:5; named only, does not act.

characters.name: Nicanor
characters.note: One of the seven chosen in Acts 6:5; named only, does not act.

characters.name: Timon
characters.note: One of the seven chosen in Acts 6:5; named only, does not act.

characters.name: Parmenas
characters.note: One of the seven chosen in Acts 6:5; named only, does not act.

characters.name: The Libertines
aliases: Cyrenians, Alexandrians and men of Cilicia and Asia
characters.note: Diaspora synagogue members who dispute with Stephen and bring him before the council (Acts 6:9-12).

characters.name: False witnesses
characters.note: Men secretly induced to accuse Stephen (Acts 6:11-13).

characters.name: Philip the evangelist
characters.note: One of the seven, who preaches in Samaria and baptizes the Ethiopian eunuch (Acts 8); later host of Paul in Caesarea (Acts 21:8); distinct from Philip the apostle.

characters.name: Simon the sorcerer
characters.note: Samaritan sorcerer who believes, offers money for the Spirit and is rebuked by Peter (Acts 8:9-24); distinct from Simon Peter and Simon the tanner.

characters.name: The Ethiopian eunuch
characters.note: Court official of Candace, queen of Ethiopia, reading Isaiah in his chariot and baptized by Philip (Acts 8:27-39).

characters.name: Candace
characters.note: Queen of the Ethiopians, named only as the eunuch's mistress (Acts 8:27); does not appear on stage.

characters.name: Saul
characters.note: Pharisee persecutor who consents to Stephen's death, is converted on the road to Damascus, then becomes the apostle Paul; the main figure from Acts 7 onward.

characters.name: Ananias of Damascus
characters.note: Disciple at Damascus who receives Saul's sight in a vision (Acts 9:10-19); distinct from Ananias the husband of Sapphira.

characters.name: Barnabas
characters.note: Cypriot Levite who sells land (Acts 4:36), vouches for Saul, and travels with Paul on the first journey; distinct from John Mark, his cousin.

characters.name: Aeneas
characters.note: Paralyzed man at Lydda healed by Peter (Acts 9:33-34).

characters.name: Tabitha
characters.note: Disciple of Joppa known for good works, raised from death by Peter (Acts 9:36-41).

characters.name: Simon the tanner
characters.note: Tanner in Joppa with whose house Peter lodges (Acts 9:43, 10:6); distinct from Simon Peter and Simon the sorcerer.

characters.name: Cornelius
characters.note: Roman centurion of the Italian Regiment in Caesarea, a devout God-fearer whose vision brings Peter to his house (Acts 10).

characters.name: Cornelius's servants and soldier
aliases: two household servants and a devout soldier
characters.note: Men sent by Cornelius to fetch Peter (Acts 10:7-8, 17-23).

characters.name: King Herod
characters.note: King who kills James son of Zebedee, imprisons Peter, and is struck dead by an angel (Acts 12); distinct from Herod Antipas of the Gospels and from Agrippa II.

characters.name: Rhoda
characters.note: Servant girl at Mary's house who recognizes Peter's voice (Acts 12:13-15).

characters.name: Mary the mother of John Mark
characters.note: Woman in Jerusalem whose house hosts the praying believers (Acts 12:12); distinct from Mary the mother of Jesus.

characters.name: John Mark
characters.note: Companion of Barnabas and Paul who leaves them in Pamphylia (Acts 12:25, 13:5, 13:13, 15:37-39); distinct from John the apostle.

characters.name: Blastus
characters.note: Court official who mediates between Herod and the people of Tyre and Sidon (Acts 12:20); does not speak.

characters.name: People of Tyre and Sidon
characters.note: Delegation seeking peace with Herod (Acts 12:20).

characters.name: Prophets and teachers of Antioch
characters.note: Group of named leaders in Antioch who set apart Barnabas and Saul (Acts 13:1-3).

characters.name: Simeon called Niger
characters.note: Antioch prophet named only in Acts 13:1.

characters.name: Lucius of Cyrene
characters.note: Antioch prophet named only in Acts 13:1.

characters.name: Manaen
aliases: foster brother of Herod the tetrarch
characters.note: Antioch prophet named only in Acts 13:1.

characters.name: Elymas Bar-Jesus
characters.note: Jewish sorcerer in Paphos who opposes Paul and is struck blind (Acts 13:6-11).

characters.name: Sergius Paulus
characters.note: Roman proconsul of Cyprus who believes after witnessing the blinding of Elymas (Acts 13:7-12).

characters.name: Judas called Barsabbas
characters.note: Chief man among the brothers sent with Silas from Jerusalem to Antioch (Acts 15:22, 27, 32); distinct from Judas Iscariot.

characters.name: Silas
characters.note: Leading brother from Jerusalem who becomes Paul's companion on the second journey (Acts 15:22-18:5); also a prophet.

characters.name: Timothy
characters.note: Young disciple of Lystra, son of a Jewish mother and Greek father, circumcised by Paul and joins him (Acts 16:1-3, 17:14-15, 18:5, 19:22, 20:4).

characters.name: Lydia
aliases: a seller of purple from Thyatira
characters.note: Dealer in purple cloth in Philippi who hears Paul by the river and is baptized with her household (Acts 16:14-15, 40).

characters.name: Slave girl with a spirit of divination
aliases: the girl with a python spirit
characters.note: Fortune-telling slave in Philippi whose spirit Paul exorcises (Acts 16:16-18).

characters.name: Her masters
aliases: the masters of the slave girl
characters.note: Owners who profit from the slave girl and drag Paul and Silas to the magistrates (Acts 16:16-24).

characters.name: The magistrates of Philippi
characters.note: City magistrates who order Paul and Silas beaten and later release them (Acts 16:20-39).

characters.name: The Philippian jailer
characters.note: Jailer who is converted after the earthquake and washes the apostles' wounds (Acts 16:27-34).

characters.name: Jason
characters.note: Host in Thessalonica whose house is attacked by a mob and who is brought before the city rulers (Acts 17:5-9); distinct from Jason in Acts 17 only in name identity question with no other Jason.

characters.name: Thessalonian Jewish mob
characters.note: Crowd who riot against Paul and Silas in Thessalonica and follow them to Beroea (Acts 17:5-13).

characters.name: Dionysius the Areopagite
characters.note: Athenian who believes after Paul's Areopagus speech (Acts 17:34).

characters.name: Damaris
characters.note: Woman of Athens who believes after Paul's Areopagus speech (Acts 17:34).

characters.name: Epicurean and Stoic philosophers
characters.note: Philosophers and citizens of Athens who debate with Paul and hear him at the Areopagus (Acts 17:18-32).

characters.name: Aquila
characters.note: Jewish tentmaker from Pontus, expelled from Rome, who works and lodges with Paul in Corinth (Acts 18:2-3, 18-26).

characters.name: Priscilla
characters.note: Wife of Aquila, tentmaker, who with her husband instructs Apollos in Ephesus (Acts 18:2, 18, 26).

characters.name: Crispus
characters.note: Ruler of the Corinthian synagogue who believes with his household (Acts 18:8).

characters.name: Justus
characters.note: Corinthian host next door to the synagogue (Acts 18:7); distinct from Joseph called Justus.

characters.name: Gallio
characters.note: Roman proconsul of Achaia who refuses to judge Paul's case in Corinth (Acts 18:12-17).

characters.name: Sosthenes
characters.note: Ruler of the Corinthian synagogue beaten before Gallio's seat by the Greeks (Acts 18:17); distinct from the co-author of 1 Corinthians.

characters.name: Apollos
characters.note: Eloquent Alexandrian preacher instructed by Priscilla and Aquila at Ephesus and sent to Achaia (Acts 18:24-28).

characters.name: Twelve disciples of John at Ephesus
characters.note: Disciples who know only John's baptism and receive the Spirit from Paul (Acts 19:1-7).

characters.name: Seven sons of Sceva
characters.note: Jewish exorcists who invoke Jesus and are attacked by a possessed man (Acts 19:13-16).

characters.name: Sceva
characters.note: Father of the seven exorcist sons; named only (Acts 19:14).

characters.name: The man with the evil spirit
characters.note: Man at Ephesus who overpowers the seven exorcists (Acts 19:16).

characters.name: Demetrius
characters.note: Silversmith of Ephesus who makes silver shrines of Artemis and incites the riot (Acts 19:24-27).

characters.name: Silversmiths and craftsmen of Ephesus
characters.note: Trade guild that riots in the theater crying for Artemis (Acts 19:24-34).

characters.name: Gaius of Macedonia
characters.note: Macedonian companion of Paul seized in the Ephesian theater riot (Acts 19:29); distinct from Gaius of Derbe.

characters.name: Aristarchus
characters.note: Macedonian travel companion seized with Gaius in Ephesus (Acts 19:29), later with Paul to Rome (Acts 27:2).

characters.name: Alexander
characters.note: Jew pushed forward by the Jews to speak to the Ephesian crowd (Acts 19:33).

characters.name: The Ephesian crowd
characters.note: Crowd that fills the theater crying 'Great is Artemis of the Ephesians' (Acts 19:29-34).

characters.name: The town clerk
characters.note: Official who calms the Ephesian crowd and dismisses the assembly (Acts 19:35-41).

characters.name: Asiarchs
characters.note: Provincial officials, friends of Paul, who beg him not to enter the theater (Acts 19:31).

characters.name: Sopater of Beroea
characters.note: Companion of Paul traveling to Asia (Acts 20:4).

characters.name: Secundus
characters.note: Thessalonian companion of Paul listed in Acts 20:4.

characters.name: Gaius of Derbe
characters.note: Companion of Paul from Derbe listed in Acts 20:4; distinct from Gaius of Macedonia.

characters.name: Tychicus
characters.note: Asian companion of Paul listed in Acts 20:4; named only.

characters.name: Trophimus
characters.note: Ephesian companion of Paul whom Jews wrongly think Paul brought into the temple (Acts 20:4, 21:29).

characters.name: Eutychus
characters.note: Young man who falls from a window during Paul's long speech at Troas and is restored (Acts 20:9-12).

characters.name: Elders of Ephesus
characters.note: Church elders summoned by Paul at Miletus to hear his farewell (Acts 20:17-38).

characters.name: Agabus
characters.note: Prophet who foretells Paul's arrest in Judea and binds his own hands with Paul's belt (Acts 11:27-28, 21:10-11).

characters.name: Mnason of Cyprus
characters.note: Early disciple in Jerusalem who hosts Paul's company (Acts 21:16).

characters.name: The Jews from Asia and the temple crowd
characters.note: Jerusalem crowd who seize Paul in the temple and try to kill him (Acts 21:27-36).

characters.name: Claudius Lysias
characters.note: Roman commander in Jerusalem who arrests Paul, has him bound, and sends him to Felix (Acts 21:31-23:30).

characters.name: Paul's sister's son
characters.note: Nephew of Paul who warns him of the plot to kill him (Acts 23:16-22).

characters.name: Julius
aliases: the centurion of the Augustan band
characters.note: Centurion who escorts Paul to Rome and treats him kindly (Acts 27:1-44).

characters.name: Sailors and soldiers of the ship
aliases: the master and owner of the ship
characters.note: Crew and soldiers aboard the ship to Italy (Acts 27).

characters.name: Ananias the high priest
characters.note: High priest who orders Paul struck before the council (Acts 23:2) and comes to Caesarea with Tertullus (Acts 24:1); distinct from Ananias of Damascus and Ananias husband of Sapphira.

characters.name: Pharisees and Sadducees
characters.note: Rival parties in the council who quarrel over the resurrection (Acts 23:6-10).

characters.name: The forty men under a curse
characters.note: Jews who bind themselves under an oath to kill Paul (Acts 23:12-21).

characters.name: Felix
characters.note: Roman governor of Judea at Caesarea who keeps Paul in custody and hears him with his wife Drusilla (Acts 23:24-24:27).

characters.name: Drusilla
characters.note: Jewish wife of Felix who hears Paul about faith in Christ (Acts 24:24).

characters.name: Tertullus
characters.note: Lawyer who prosecutes Paul before Felix for the high priest (Acts 24:1-8).

characters.name: Porcius Festus
characters.note: Roman governor succeeding Felix, who hears Paul's appeal to Caesar and consults Agrippa (Acts 24:27-26:32).

characters.name: King Agrippa
characters.note: Jewish king who hears Paul's defense with his sister Bernice (Acts 25:13-26:32); distinct from Herod Agrippa I.

characters.name: Bernice
characters.note: Sister of King Agrippa who accompanies him to hear Paul (Acts 25:13, 23; 26:30).

characters.name: Caesar
characters.note: Roman emperor to whom Paul appeals; does not appear on stage.

characters.name: The natives of Malta
characters.note: Islanders who kindle a fire for the shipwrecked and watch the viper incident (Acts 28:1-6).

characters.name: Publius
aliases: the chief man of the island
characters.note: Chief man of Malta who hosts Paul for three days and whose father Paul heals (Acts 28:7-8).

characters.name: Brothers of Rome
characters.note: Believers of Puteoli and Rome who meet Paul on the road (Acts 28:14-15).

characters.name: Leaders of the Jews in Rome
characters.note: Jewish leaders in Rome who hear Paul explain himself and debate (Acts 28:17-29).

characters.name: Isaiah
characters.note: Prophet quoted by Paul and by the Ethiopian eunuch's scroll (Acts 8:28-35, 28:25); does not appear on stage.

characters.name: David
characters.note: Israelite king quoted in Peter's speeches (Acts 1:16, 2:25-34); does not appear on stage.

characters.name: Abraham
characters.note: Patriarch recounted by Stephen (Acts 7:2-8); does not appear on stage.

characters.name: Moses
characters.note: Lawgiver recounted in Stephen's speech (Acts 7:20-44); does not appear on stage except as a voice in Stephen's account.

characters.name: Joseph the patriarch
characters.note: Son of Jacob sold into Egypt, recounted by Stephen (Acts 7:9-18); does not appear on stage.

characters.name: Pharaoh
characters.note: Egyptian ruler in Stephen's account; does not appear on stage.

characters.name: Samuel
characters.note: Prophet named in Paul's and Peter's speeches; does not appear on stage.

characters.name: John the Baptist
characters.note: Baptizer mentioned in Acts 1, 10, 11, 13; does not appear on stage.

characters.name: Judas the Galilean
characters.note: See judas_of_galilee; duplicate reference, not separate.

characters.name: Pontius Pilate
characters.note: Roman governor who handed Jesus over; named in Peter's speeches and prayer; does not appear on stage.

characters.name: Ananias (high priest of Acts 4)
characters.note: Possibly the same high priest as Annas; kept separate because the text names only Annas here.

characters.name: Cornelius the centurion of the Italian cohort
characters.note: Duplicate of Cornelius; same person.

characters.name: Peter and John
characters.note: Pair of apostles who act together in Acts 3-4 and 8; see individual entries.

characters.name: Herod the tetrarch
characters.note: Tetrarch named in Acts 4:27 and 13:1; does not appear on stage.

characters.name: Diaspora Jews and proselytes of Antioch
characters.note: Antioch-in-Pisidia synagogue audience who follow Paul and Barnabas (Acts 13:43).

characters.name: Jews of Antioch and Iconium
aliases: the Jews from Antioch and Iconium
characters.note: Opponents who stone Paul at Lystra (Acts 14:19).

characters.name: The crowd of Lystra
characters.note: Crowd who wish to sacrifice to Barnabas and Paul as gods (Acts 14:11-18).

characters.name: The priest of Jupiter
characters.note: Priest who brings oxen and garlands to the gates of Lystra (Acts 14:13).

characters.name: The lame man at Lystra
aliases: a cripple from his mother's womb
characters.note: Crippled man healed by Paul at Lystra (Acts 14:8-10).

characters.name: Judas and Silas
characters.note: Pair sent with the letter; see individual entries.

characters.name: The apostles and elders of Jerusalem
characters.note: Jerusalem leaders who write the decree of Acts 15 and send delegates; a group that acts as one.

characters.name: Believing Pharisees
aliases: some of the sect of the Pharisees who believed
characters.note: Pharisee believers who insist on circumcision (Acts 15:5).

characters.name: Men from Judea
aliases: some men who came down from Judea
characters.note: Visitors who teach circumcision at Antioch (Acts 15:1).

characters.name: Lydia's household
characters.note: Household baptized with Lydia (Acts 16:15).

characters.name: The jailer's household
characters.note: Household baptized with the jailer (Acts 16:33).

characters.name: The Jews of Beroea
characters.note: Synagogue audience in Beroea who examine the Scriptures (Acts 17:10-12).

characters.name: Jews of Thessalonica
characters.note: Thessalonian opponents who come to Beroea to stir up the crowd (Acts 17:13).

characters.name: The Corinthian believers
characters.note: Corinthians who hear and are baptized (Acts 18:8).

characters.name: Ephesian Jews
characters.note: Synagogue audience in Ephesus who ask Paul to stay (Acts 18:19-20).

characters.name: Hardened listeners at Ephesus
characters.note: Opponents who speak evil of the Way (Acts 19:9); same as Ephesian Jews group.

characters.name: Believers who confess their deeds
characters.note: Believers who bring their magic books to burn (Acts 19:18-19).

characters.name: Practitioners of magical arts
characters.note: Ephesians who burn their books (Acts 19:19).

characters.name: Disciples at Troas
aliases: the disciples gathered to break bread
characters.note: Congregation at Troas listening to Paul's late-night teaching (Acts 20:7-12).

characters.name: The centurion and his guard
aliases: the centurion who delivered the prisoners
characters.note: Officials who deliver prisoners to Rome (Acts 28:16).

characters.name: The Augustan band
characters.note: Military unit to which Julius belongs; does not act as a group.

characters.name: The viper
characters.note: Snake that fastens on Paul's hand on Malta (Acts 28:3-5).

characters.name: The crowd who stone Stephen
characters.note: Jews who cast Stephen out of the city and stone him (Acts 7:57-60).

characters.name: The witnesses to the stoning
characters.note: Men who lay their garments at the feet of Saul (Acts 7:58).

characters.name: The seven chosen to serve tables
characters.note: Group chosen by the Twelve in Acts 6:3-6; see individuals Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, Nicolaus.

characters.name: Cyrenians and Alexandrians
characters.note: Jews from Cyrene and Alexandria in the synagogue dispute with Stephen (Acts 6:9); also in the crowd of Acts 2.

characters.name: Jews of Damascus
aliases: the Jews who lived at Damascus
characters.note: Opponents who plot to kill Saul at Damascus (Acts 9:23-25).

characters.name: The chief priests
characters.note: Authorities who give Saul letters to arrest believers (Acts 9:1-2, 14, 26:10).

characters.name: Disciples of Damascus
characters.note: Believers who lower Saul in a basket from the wall (Acts 9:25).

characters.name: The men traveling with Saul
characters.note: Companions who hear the voice but see no one on the road (Acts 9:7; 22:9; 26:14).

characters.name: Herod's soldiers
characters.note: Soldiers guarding Peter in prison (Acts 12:4-19).

characters.name: People of Lydda and Sharon
characters.note: Residents who turn to the Lord after Aeneas is healed (Acts 9:35).

characters.name: The widows of Joppa
characters.note: Widows who weep and show the garments Tabitha made (Acts 9:39).

characters.name: Cornelius's relatives and near friends
characters.note: Gathering in Cornelius's house (Acts 10:24, 27).

characters.name: Circumcised believers
characters.note: Jewish believers who object to Peter's visit to the Gentiles (Acts 10:45; 11:2).

characters.name: Men of Cyprus and Cyrene in Antioch
aliases: some of them men of Cyprus and Cyrene
characters.note: Unnamed evangelists who preach to Greeks at Antioch (Acts 11:20).

characters.name: Visitors from Phoenicia and Samaria
characters.note: Travel companions who report the conversion of the Gentiles (Acts 15:3).

locations.name: Mount of Olives
locations.note: Hill near Jerusalem from which Jesus ascends (Acts 1:12).  Also where the disciples return.  ## Note: placed here as the site of the ascension.  ## See 1:9-12.  ## Stub for setting.  ##.  ## Mountain near Jerusalem.

locations.name: Jerusalem
locations.note: Main city of action in Acts 1-8, the seat of the apostles, temple and council; later the place of Paul's arrest (Acts 21-23).

locations.name: Upper room in Jerusalem
aliases: the upper room where they were staying
locations.note: Room where the eleven and the women gather to pray (Acts 1:13), and where the Spirit comes at Pentecost (Acts 2:1-2).

locations.name: The temple in Jerusalem
locations.note: Temple courts where Peter and John heal the lame man, the apostles preach, and Paul is seized (Acts 3-5, 21).

locations.name: The Beautiful Gate
locations.note: Gate of the temple where the lame man is laid (Acts 3:2, 10).

locations.name: Solomon's porch
aliases: the porch that is called Solomon's
locations.note: Colonnade of the temple where the crowd gathers around Peter (Acts 3:11, 5:12).

locations.name: Akeldama, the field of blood
aliases: the field bought with the reward of wickedness
locations.note: Field Judas acquired (Acts 1:18-19); referred to in speech, not shown as a setting.

locations.name: Damascus
locations.note: City where Saul is converted, blinded and baptized; later where he preaches and escapes (Acts 9, 22, 26).

locations.name: Straight Street in Damascus
aliases: the street which is called Straight
locations.note: Street where Saul lodges and Ananias finds him (Acts 9:11).

locations.name: Joppa
locations.note: Port town where Tabitha dies and is raised; where Peter stays with Simon the tanner and receives his vision (Acts 9:36-10:23).

locations.name: Caesarea
locations.note: Roman port and administrative seat; home of Cornelius, Philip, Herod's palace where Paul is held (Acts 8:40, 10, 12:19, 21:8, 23-26).

locations.name: Lydda
locations.note: Town where Peter heals Aeneas (Acts 9:32-35).

locations.name: Cornelius's house
locations.note: House in Caesarea where Peter preaches and the Spirit falls on the Gentiles (Acts 10:24-48).

locations.name: Simon the tanner's house by the sea
locations.note: House by the seaside in Joppa where Peter lodges and goes up to the roof to pray (Acts 9:43, 10:6-9).

locations.name: The housetop in Joppa
locations.note: Roof where Peter sees the vision of the sheet (Acts 10:9-16).

locations.name: Antioch in Syria
locations.note: Church in Syria where believers are first called Christians, where Paul and Barnabas are set apart (Acts 11:19-30, 13:1-3, 14:26-28, 15:30-35).

locations.name: Islands of the Aegean (Chios, Samos, Cos, Rhodes)
locations.note: Ports on Paul's return voyage (Acts 20:15, 21:1).

locations.name: Herod's palace in Caesarea
locations.note: Palace where Felix and Festus hold Paul in custody and Agrippa hears him (Acts 23:35, 25:23).

locations.name: The prison in Jerusalem
locations.note: Prison where Peter is held and freed by an angel (Acts 12:4-11).

locations.name: The iron gate to the city
aliases: the iron gate that leads into the city
locations.note: Gate that opens by itself for Peter's escape (Acts 12:10).

locations.name: House of Mary the mother of John Mark
locations.note: Jerusalem house where believers gather to pray; Peter knocks at the gate (Acts 12:12-17).

locations.name: The council chamber in Jerusalem
locations.note: Meeting place of the Sanhedrin where Peter and John, Stephen and Paul are judged (Acts 4:15, 5:27, 6:12, 22:30, 23:1).

locations.name: Synagogue of the Libertines
locations.note: Synagogue in Jerusalem where Stephen debates the diaspora Jews (Acts 6:9).

locations.name: Samaria
locations.note: City and region where Philip preaches and Peter and John come to lay hands on converts (Acts 8:4-25).

locations.name: The road from Jerusalem to Gaza
aliases: the way that goes down to Gaza
locations.note: Wilderness road where Philip meets the Ethiopian eunuch (Acts 8:26-39).

locations.name: The eunuch's chariot
locations.note: Chariot on the desert road where the eunuch reads Isaiah and is baptized (Acts 8:28-38).

locations.name: Water beside the road
locations.note: Place on the desert road where the eunuch is baptized (Acts 8:36-38).

locations.name: Azotus
locations.note: Town where Philip reappears after the Spirit takes him (Acts 8:40).

locations.name: The riverside outside Philippi
aliases: the place of prayer by the river
locations.note: Riverbank outside the gate where Paul speaks to women and Lydia is baptized (Acts 16:13).

locations.name: Philippi
locations.note: Roman colony where Lydia, the slave girl, Paul and Silas, and the jailer appear (Acts 16:12-40).

locations.name: The prison at Philippi
locations.note: Inner prison where Paul and Silas are held in stocks and freed by earthquake (Acts 16:23-34).

locations.name: The marketplace of Philippi
locations.note: Public square where Paul and Silas are dragged before the magistrates (Acts 16:19).

locations.name: Thessalonica
locations.note: City with a Jewish synagogue where Paul preaches three Sabbaths and Jason's house is attacked (Acts 17:1-9).

locations.name: Jason's house in Thessalonica
locations.note: House attacked by the mob (Acts 17:5).

locations.name: Beroea
locations.note: City where Jews examine the Scriptures daily and believe (Acts 17:10-14).

locations.name: Athens
locations.note: City full of idols where Paul debates in the synagogue and marketplace (Acts 17:16-34).

locations.name: The Areopagus
locations.note: Hill and council place in Athens where Paul speaks about the unknown god (Acts 17:19-34).

locations.name: Corinth
locations.note: City where Paul lives eighteen months with Aquila and Priscilla and faces the case before Gallio (Acts 18:1-17).

locations.name: House of Justus next to the synagogue in Corinth
locations.note: House beside the synagogue where Paul teaches (Acts 18:7).

locations.name: The judgment seat at Corinth
locations.note: Court where Gallio dismisses the charges against Paul (Acts 18:12-17).

locations.name: Cenchreae
locations.note: Port near Corinth where Paul shaves his head for a vow (Acts 18:18).

locations.name: Ephesus
locations.note: City where Paul spends two years, the sons of Sceva are beaten, and the silversmith riot occurs (Acts 18:19-19:41).

locations.name: School of Tyrannus
locations.note: Lecture hall in Ephesus where Paul reasons daily (Acts 19:9).

locations.name: The theater at Ephesus
locations.note: Theater where the silversmiths' mob gathers and cries for Artemis (Acts 19:29-41).

locations.name: Temple of Artemis at Ephesus
aliases: the temple of the great goddess Artemis
locations.note: Great temple whose shrines and worship are threatened (Acts 19:27).

locations.name: Macedonia
locations.note: Region visited by Paul on his journeys, including Philippi, Thessalonica and Beroea (Acts 16:9-17:14, 19:21-20:3).

locations.name: Troas
locations.note: Port where Paul receives the Macedonian vision and where Eutychus falls from the window (Acts 16:8, 20:5-12).

locations.name: Upper room at Troas
aliases: the upper room where we were gathered
locations.note: Room with many lamps where Paul speaks late and Eutychus falls (Acts 20:7-9).

locations.name: Miletus
locations.note: Port where Paul meets the Ephesian elders for farewell (Acts 20:15-38).

locations.name: Tyre
locations.note: Port where Paul's company stays seven days and the believers pray on the beach (Acts 21:3-6).

locations.name: The beach at Tyre
locations.note: Shore where Paul kneels with the disciples and they pray (Acts 21:5).

locations.name: Ptolemais
locations.note: Port where the company greets the brothers for one day (Acts 21:7).

locations.name: Court of the temple
locations.note: Place where Paul is seized by the Asian Jews and nearly killed (Acts 21:27-36).

locations.name: The Roman barracks
locations.note: Roman fortress where Paul is taken under guard (Acts 21:34-37, 22:24, 23:10, 16).

locations.name: Stairs of the fortress
locations.note: Steps from which Paul addresses the crowd in Hebrew (Acts 21:40-22:21).

locations.name: Antipatris
locations.note: Stop on the night road from Jerusalem to Caesarea (Acts 23:31).

locations.name: Fair Havens near Lasea, Crete
locations.note: Harbor on Crete where the ship stays and Paul gives advice (Acts 27:8-12).

locations.name: The ship bound for Italy
locations.note: Ship carrying Paul and the prisoners to Italy, wrecked near Malta (Acts 27:1-44).

locations.name: Malta
locations.note: Island where the ship is wrecked and Paul heals the father of Publius (Acts 28:1-10).

locations.name: Syracuse, Rhegium, Puteoli
locations.note: Ports on the Italian voyage (Acts 28:12-14).

locations.name: Rome
locations.note: Paul's final destination where he is held under guard in his rented house and preaches freely (Acts 28:14-31).

locations.name: The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns
locations.note: Roadside stops where Roman brothers meet Paul (Acts 28:15).

locations.name: Paul's rented house in Rome
locations.note: House where Paul receives visitors for two years (Acts 28:30).

locations.name: Tarsus
locations.note: Paul's birthplace, to which he is sent away from Jerusalem by the brothers (Acts 9:11, 30; 11:25; 21:39; 22:3).

locations.name: Gaza
locations.note: City at the end of the desert road from Jerusalem (Acts 8:26).

locations.name: Cyprus
locations.note: Island visited by Barnabas and Paul; home of Barnabas and Mnason (Acts 4:36, 11:20, 13:4-12, 15:39, 21:16).

locations.name: Salamis and Paphos
locations.note: Cypriot cities visited by Barnabas, Paul and John Mark, where Elymas is blinded (Acts 13:5-12).

locations.name: Perga in Pamphylia
locations.note: Cities where John Mark leaves the missionaries and where they preach (Acts 13:13, 14:25).

locations.name: Antioch of Pisidia
locations.note: Synagogue city where Paul preaches a long sermon on the Sabbath (Acts 13:14-52).

locations.name: Iconium
locations.note: City of Lycaonia where Paul and Barnabas preach, are opposed and flee (Acts 13:51-14:6).

locations.name: Lystra
locations.note: City of Lycaonia where Paul heals the lame man and is stoned (Acts 14:6-20; 16:1-2).

locations.name: Derbe
locations.note: City of Lycaonia where Paul and Barnabas make many disciples (Acts 14:6, 20; 16:1; 20:4).

locations.name: Lycaonia
locations.note: Region including Lystra, Derbe and Iconium where Paul is taken for Hermes (Acts 14:6-11).

locations.name: Phrygia and Galatia

locations.note: Regions traversed by Paul on the journeys (Acts 16:6, 18:23).

locations.name: Mysia and Bithynia
locations.note: Regions Paul is forbidden to enter (Acts 16:7-8).

locations.name: Asia
locations.note: Roman province where Paul is forbidden to speak and later ministers in Ephesus (Acts 16:6, 19:10, 20:18).

locations.name: Judea
locations.note: Region in which the disciples are scattered and to which Paul is sent by the Spirit's wider commission (Acts 1:8, 8:1, 9:31, 11:1, 26:20).

locations.name: Galilee
locations.note: Region where the apostles are from; mentioned as the place from which Peter's audience comes and the men who witnessed Jesus (Acts 1:11, 2:7, 9:31, 10:37).

locations.name: Egypt
locations.note: Land of Joseph and Moses' exodus, recounted by Stephen and Paul (Acts 7:9-39, 13:17).

locations.name: Mount Sinai
locations.note: Mountain where the angel speaks to Moses in the bush (Acts 7:30-38).

locations.name: Mesopotamia and Haran
locations.note: Places where God calls Abraham (Acts 7:2-4).

locations.name: Shechem
locations.note: Place where Jacob and the fathers are buried (Acts 7:16); referred to in speech.

locations.name: Babylon
locations.note: Place of exile in Stephen's quotation (Acts 7:43); referred to in speech.

locations.name: The wilderness
locations.note: Desert where Israel wanders forty years in Stephen's and Paul's speeches (Acts 7:36, 42; 13:18); referred to in speech.

locations.name: The burning bush
locations.note: Place of the angel's appearance to Moses (Acts 7:30-33).

locations.name: Roman provinces of Achaia and Macedonia
locations.note: Provinces through which Paul travels to Corinth and Achaia (Acts 18:12, 19:21, 20:2-3).

locations.name: Italy
locations.note: Region toward which Paul is sent, and from which Aquila and Priscilla came (Acts 18:2, 27:1).

locations.name: The sea
aliases: the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia
locations.note: Several seas referred to in the narrative, including the sea of the shipwreck (Acts 27:27) and the Red Sea (Acts 7:36).

locations.name: Outside the city wall of Jerusalem
locations.note: Place where Stephen is stoned after being cast out (Acts 7:58).

locations.name: The wall of Damascus
locations.note: Wall through which Saul is lowered in a basket (Acts 9:25).

locations.name: Gate of Damascus
locations.note: Gate watched by the Jews who plot to kill Saul (Acts 9:24).

locations.name: Shipwreck site near the island
locations.note: Coast where the ship runs aground and the passengers reach land (Acts 27:39-44).

locations.name: Hall of hearing in Caesarea
locations.note: Official hall where Festus brings Paul before Agrippa and Bernice (Acts 25:23).

locations.name: The judgment seat in Caesarea
locations.note: Tribunal where Festus sits and Paul is brought (Acts 25:6, 17).

locations.name: Gate of the temple
locations.note: Temple gate where Peter and John meet the lame man (Acts 3:2; cf. Beautiful Gate); included for the setting of Acts 3.

locations.name: The house of Philip the evangelist
locations.note: Caesarean house where Paul stays with Philip and his four prophesying daughters (Acts 21:8-10).

locations.name: House where the apostles met
aliases: the apostles and elders' meeting place
locations.note: Place in Jerusalem where the council of Acts 15 is held; not separately named in the text.

locations.name: House of Judas in Damascus
locations.note: House on Straight Street where Saul is kept three days blind (Acts 9:11).

brief.tone: Hopeful and urgent: a young movement spreading outward from Jerusalem, marked by miracles, fierce opposition, courtroom tension, and quiet communal devotion.
depiction_rules: Depict the risen Jesus only in the Acts 1 ascension and in Saul's vision; do not show a face or body for God the Father, only light, cloud or a hand.
The Holy Spirit appears as wind, tongues of fire or a dove-like presence, not as a human figure.
Angels appear as men in white or bright clothing, as the text describes them.
Show miracles (healing, the earthquake, the viper) as events in the scene, not as spectacle; avoid gore in the stoning and the death of Ananias and Sapphira beyond the implied moment.
Avoid depicting Judas's death in detail; the text describes it only in speech.
Show the crowds at Ephesus and Jerusalem as agitated but not caricatured.

era.name: First-century Roman Empire, c. AD 30-62, from Jerusalem and Judea to Rome
era.people: Jews of Galilee and Judea, Hellenistic Jews of the diaspora, Samaritans, Greeks, Romans, Cypriots, Lycaonians, Ethiopians, and islanders of Malta; Roman officials, soldiers and sailors; many languages in use.
era.dress: Robes and cloaks (himation, tunics), head coverings for men and women, sandals, belts, military Roman tunics and cloaks for soldiers, white garments for angels and priests, sailors in short tunics.
era.buildings_and_objects: Jerusalem temple and its porches and gates, synagogues, upper rooms with lamps, Roman barracks and governors' palaces such as Herod's palace at Caesarea, city gates and walls, Greek theaters and temples (Artemis at Ephesus), ships with sails and anchors, chariots, scrolls and letters.
era.technology: Sailing ships and oared vessels, lamps and oil light, carts and chariots, scrolls and written letters, no printing, no firearms, no mechanical clocks; time reckoned by hours of the day.
